description:
FILED s418c from a live observation (USER): during a full sweep, one
`perl pl2cl --server` process reached ~10 GB RSS before ending normally.
The run was unharmed (sweep GATE clean), but a transpile server that big is
either (a) MONOTONIC GROWTH across requests â PPI documents / OpcodeTree
node trees / Environment state retained per file and never freed, so a long
sweep accumulates hundreds of files worth â or (b) one pathological file
(the op/cond.t family is excluded for exactly that).  (a) is the likely
one for a server.

THE CHEAP DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (do this first, ~10 min): start one
server, feed it the same SMALL file N times, and read RSS after each â flat
means (b) and the task retargets at finding the file; growing means (a) and
the fix is freeing per-request state (find what holds the reference: the
PPI Document, the node tree, a memo table keyed by file).  Note perl rarely
returns freed memory to the OS, so measure growth BETWEEN requests of equal
input, not absolute size.

Context: the sweep runs 108+ files through server transpiles; 10 GB on a
13.5 GB box is close to the OOM line the --jobs guidance already respects
(#160, s399).  A leak fix would also speed the sweep (less paging).
title: pl2cl --server reached 10 GB RSS during a sweep â measure: leak-per-request or one file?
